What if I could show to you by some time-travelling device that if you gave your child a horrible, horrible disease that they were going to manage to overcome it and they got lots of good things out of it, they became a strong character, would you be okay with me injecting that disease into them? I think not. Even if you were in a position of omniscience to know that once they were capable of getting through it and once they'd gone through it they'd develop certain virtues, I think you'd still rather say no, I'd rather not have my child go through that even...

And you said that you didn't have omniscience. When I asked you about that, you said, well, I'm not in a position of omnipotence and omniscience. And I'm giving you that opportunity. I'm saying here's an example where as a time traveler.
You can have that omniscience and know that your child will overcome it and will be a better person for it, but you still say that you wouldn't inflict it upon them and you've got to ask yourself why not? Because there's a difference between when something happens in part of like a random chaotic universe versus the actual action of inflicting the pain.
